properties.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet,
move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties.
People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean.
Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from recent high surf events will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 16 at 8:29AM PST until November 16 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.instruction:
Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 16 at 2:57PM PST until November 16 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast early next week due to a combination of northerly
winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream heavy
rainfall working north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 6:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 6:30 PM EST Saturday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 2.6 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

Persons are urged to stay indoors until conditions improve. If you
must go outside, dress in layers. Several layers of clothes will keep

cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:30 AM PST Sunday the stage was 16.7 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 5:30 AM PST Sunday was 16.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 17.1 feet
late this morning. It will then fall below flood stage late
tonight.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10
to 15 feet increasing to 15 to 18 feet with local sets to 20
feet. Dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 9 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The High Surf Advisory may need to be
extended through Wednesday, and another round of larger surf
is expected Thursday into Friday.
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 16 at 4:14AM PST until November 17 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Brevard, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise to Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to continue to remain steady with slight deviations
in river levels through mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Monday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Monday was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 17.1 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast through at least midweek due to a combination of
northerly winds and water from upstream heavy rainfall working north
through the basin. Rises to Moderate Flood Stage are forecast later
in the week due to the heavy rainfall expected.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor to Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor to moderate flooding
is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.possible

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Monday was 2.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to rise slightly through minor
flood stage into mid-week, possibly reaching moderate flood stage
by late week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to
25 to 30 feet. Waves and surf gradually diminish but remain
hazardous through this evening.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and
other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor beach erosion
may damage coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal
water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning.
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 16 at 8:12AM PST until November 16 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

properties.instruction:

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 15 at 5:07AM PST until November 16 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 10 to 151 feet with dangerous
rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will
create an extended period of large surf this week, with the
potential for WARNING level surf Wednesday and Thursday. Areas
that may see most significant impacts will be west- northwest
facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying
areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the
Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor
entrance.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and hazardous surf conditions. Breakers up to
25 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Minor
beach erosion may damage coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock
people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid
ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning.
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 16 at 12:30AM PST until November 16 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.instruction:

producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can easily lift or roll logs which can injure or kill
someone caught in their path.

* WHEN...For the Cold Weather Advisory, from 10 PM this evening to 8

PST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result. Cold
conditions will be hazardous, especially for vulnerable
populations. Prolonged exposure will lead to hypothermia for people
and animals.
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 16 at 1:40PM PST until November 18 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Ensure portable heaters are working properly and are used correctly
to avoid sparking a fire indoors. Do not use generators or grills
inside as carbon monoxide poisoning can result.

Check with your local, city, or county officials for information on
available warming centers.

Be sure to dress in layers if outdoors. Make sure that pets and
livestock have adequate food, unfrozen water, and warmth. Cover or
tend to sensitive crops, plants, and vegetation.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, slight rises within Minor Flood
Stage are forecast this weekend into next week due to a combination
of northerly winds, downstream tidal effects, and water from upstream
heavy rainfall working north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EST Saturday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.4 feet just after
midnight tonight. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 PM this evening to

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 17 at 1:28AM EST until November 19 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 3 AM PST Sunday. For
the High Surf Advisory, from 3 AM Sunday to 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an
exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal
structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells
will create an extended period of large surf into next week,
with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday
night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant
impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with
widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at
Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo
Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to
12 feet. Occasional larger sets may occur near Ventura Harbor.
Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas that are normally dry,
especially around the time of high tide, including over beach
parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible.
There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents
can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves
can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and
capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly
swells are expected to produce large surf into the week with
highest surf and greatest impacts potentially peaking again
Monday. Minor to moderate coastal flooding impacts are possible,
especially when largest surf overlaps with peak high tides.
Some of these impacts may be moderate to significant beach
erosion and shallow flooding of normally dry beaches and
walkways.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking
waves of 14 to 18 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High
Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 12 to 17 feet with local
sets to 20 feet and dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an
exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal
structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore. Minor tidal overflow during morning high
tides.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will
create an extended period of large surf this week, with the
potential for WARNING level surf Wednesday and Thursday. Areas
that may see most significant impacts will be west- northwest
facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying
areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the
Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor
entrance.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall over recent weeks has caused river levels on the St.
Johns near Geneva Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate Flood Stage.
River levels are expected to remain nearly steady this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Water enters the first story of homes on
Whitcomb Drive between Crossover Lane and Lake Harney Road. Water
covers Mullet Lake Park.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 9.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Monday was 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 9.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at
favored breakpoints. For the High Surf Advisory, Large breaking
waves of 20 to 25 ft, with occasional sets of 25 to 35 ft at
favored breakpoints.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 4 AM PST today. For the

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.

than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 10 and
18 inches above 4000 ft and winds gusting as high as 50 mph. Total
snow accumulations between 3 and 8 inches below 4000 ft and winds
gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...The Winter Storm Warning is for areas above 4000 ft,
including Snowman and Dead Horse Summits on highway 89, and Everitt
Memorial Highway and the Old SKi Bowl. The Winter Weather Advisory
includes the Interstate 5 Corridor between Black Butte Summit and
Weed, and the cities of Mount Shasta City and McCloud.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 4 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday morning and evening
commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches. Roads, and
especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and
hazardous. The strong winds and weight of snow on tree limbs may
down power lines and could cause sporadic power outages.
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 17 at 3:54AM PST until November 19 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

accumulations 2 to 7 inches, with up to 16 inches near Lassen Park.

Interstate 80, State Route 4, State Route 108, Southern Cascades
above 6000 feet, including Lassen National Park.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 10 PM PST Monday.

* IMPACTS...The hazardous conditions will impact travelers this
evening, as well as the Monday morning and evening commutes.

tonight into Monday morning. Lull in activity expected on Tuesday,
followed by a colder, stronger system by mid-week.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 12 to
18 feet lowering to 8 to 12 feet on Wednesday. For the Coastal
Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST Wednesday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 9 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The High Surf Advisory will need to be
extended beyond Wednesday and possibly through the week, with a
moderate chance of a High Surf Warning on Thursday.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall over recent weeks has caused river levels on the St.
Johns near Geneva Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate Flood Stage.
River levels are expected to remain nearly steady this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Moderate
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Water enters the first story of homes on
Whitcomb Drive between Crossover Lane and Lake Harney Road. Water
covers Mullet Lake Park.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 9.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Sunday was 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 9.0 feet
this afternoon.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
